metadata.prompt:
Key insight during implementation:

The decision_nodes table has two types of foreign key references:

NON-NULLABLE (must delete the referencing record):
- decision_edges.from_node_id / to_node_id - edges can't exist without nodes
- decision_context.node_id - context meaningless without node
- session_nodes.node_id - junction table, just delete the association

NULLABLE (set to NULL, preserve the record):
- decision_sessions.root_node_id - session can exist without a root
- command_log.decision_node_id - command history preserved even if node deleted
- roadmap_items.outcome_node_id - roadmap item exists independently

This distinction matters because:
1. Deleting edges/context/session_nodes is safe and expected
2. Deleting sessions/commands/roadmap_items would lose important data
3. Setting to NULL preserves the record but breaks the link

The implementation handles this correctly:
- diesel::delete() for non-nullable references
- diesel::update().set(column.eq::<Option<i32>>(None)) for nullable

title: Foreign key handling: nullable vs non-nullable references
